title: How Much Fiber in Split Peas? 16.3g per Cup
description: Split Peas: about 16.3 g of fiber per 1 cup, cooked (58% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in split peas?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt

intro: Split peas rank #2 of 10 beans and legumes on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in split peas by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in split peas?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt at 8.3 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, cooked; 196 g) therefore has about 16.3 g of fiber and 231 calories. That is 58% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 65% of a 25 g day and 43% of a 38 g day.
Split peas are dried peas with the skin removed and the seed split in half. They cook down into a thick purée in under an hour without soaking, and a cooked cup holds as much fiber as most beans.

sections.heading: Split peas vs split pea soup
paragraphs: Most of the fiber in split pea soup comes from the peas, but soup is mostly liquid. A typical cup of soup (the third row in the table, a site estimate for common recipes) has far less fiber than a cup of plain cooked split peas.
For homemade soup, add up the dry peas you used, then divide by servings. One cup of dry split peas yields roughly two and a half cups cooked.

sections.heading: How split peas compare with other beans and legumes
paragraphs: Of the 10 beans and legumes on this site, split peas rank #2 for fiber per typical serving and #2 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 7 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [lentils](/fiber-in-lentils) at 15.6 g (1 cup, cooked); [pinto beans](/fiber-in-pinto-beans) at 15.4 g (1 cup, cooked); [black beans](/fiber-in-black-beans) at 15 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), split peas are #13 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding split peas to your day
paragraphs: Make a thick soup with more peas than broth, or use cooked split peas as a dal-style side. They also thicken stews without flour.

Example: 1 cup split peas, 1 slice whole wheat bread, 1 carrot. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 19.9 g of fiber, with 16.3 g from the split peas. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of split peas?
faqs.a: 8.3 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Peas, split, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in split peas (1/2 cup, cooked)?
faqs.a: About 8.1 g, for 98 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.

faqs.q: Are green and yellow split peas different in fiber?
faqs.a: Not meaningfully for tracking. USDA lists a single cooked split pea entry, and labels for both colors fall in a similar range.

faqs.q: Are split peas the same as green peas?
faqs.a: They come from the same plant, but split peas are dried mature seeds, while green peas are eaten fresh or frozen. Cooked split peas are about 16.3 g (1 cup, cooked); cooked green peas are about 8.8 g (1 cup, cooked).
